A.note: The wide view does show the rock, the sea and some ships. But the camps are flat tan rectangles with tiny dark dots on a plain green plane. The trees are sparse black specks. The rock is small and distant, so the siege has no weight.

B.note: The top-down view shows regimented rows of identical white blocks on tan rectangles, like game tokens or a spreadsheet grid. A single trench line is the only real feature. There is no rock, sea or horizon, so the location can't be identified. The terrain texture is a mottled green wash.

C.note: The framing is the same as A. The vegetation is better: darker, denser tree clumps and a more varied grass texture. The sea is more natural, with a lighter horizon haze. The camps are still flat tan strips with tiny dots and no real tents or troops.

why: C has the same readable layout as A, with more natural vegetation, water and atmosphere. B has no sense of place, and its repeated white blocks look like game pieces.
top_fix_for_best: Replace the flat tan camp rectangles with textured camp ground (trampled earth, paths, tents, fires, smoke) and larger, better-modelled troop and tent clusters. Then lower the camera, or move it closer to the camps, so the besiegers' lines read at small-screen scale with the fortified rock behind them.
